solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shimmering in image around retina's start — of one perhaps

definitions.text: Shimmering in image around retina's start — of one perhaps

indicators.note: shimmering suggests something wavering and unstable, so the letters are rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter, here the opening of retina's

explanation.surface: A description of the flickering visual aura some sufferers see before a bad headache sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shimmering' rearranges IN IMAGE together with R, the start of 'retina's'. The whole clue also describes the aura that comes with one of these headaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Shimmering visual disturbance around the eyes is a classic warning symptom of this severe recurring headache.

clue.text: Model cut after motorway accident

parts.note: MI reads as M1, Britain's first major motorway

indicators.note: cut means the word is trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: to model something is to shape it

explanation.surface: A model's car crash on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, from London to Leeds. 'cut' drops the final letter, and 'after' places that piece behind the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident or misfortune, usually a minor one.

clue.text: They use axes: fruit chopped has to be hollowed out

indicators.note: chopped means the word loses its end, here its final letter

parts.note: a grape is a fruit

indicators.note: a word hollowed out keeps only its outside letters, losing the middle of has

explanation.surface: A cook chopping fruit and hollowing it out, with an axe joke thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like the plural of axe, the chopping tool, which fits 'chopped'; here it is the plural of axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Charts plotted on x and y coordinate lines rely on axes to show values.

clue.text: Backing off, agreeing to accept nothing — that'll produce noise from squeezed middle

definitions.text: that'll produce noise from squeezed middle

indicators.note: to accept means to take something in, so a letter goes inside
taking off the back of a word removes its last letter

parts.note: according means agreeing or in harmony, as in according with the facts
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A politician retreating and agreeing to nothing, appealing to the squeezed middle class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing off' drops G from ACCORDING to give ACCORDIN; 'to accept' puts O inside it. The 'squeezed middle' is a British political phrase for the hard-pressed middle classes.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument makes music when its bellows in the centre are pushed and pulled by the player.

clue.text: Toilet in all-female preserve being given handle?

parts.note: an all-female group has no men

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to cure meat or fish is to preserve it
LAT is short for latrine, a toilet

explanation.surface: A women-only nature reserve deciding what to call its toilet block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' is slang for a name, so the definition is a fair, if playful, pointer to naming.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of naming things; a handle is informal for a name, as in a nickname or username.

clue.text: Party with great chat

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for the Conservative Party in Britain
fab, short for fabulous, means great

explanation.surface: A party where you can have a great natter.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal talk or chinwag, short for confabulation.

clue.text: Old climber like Jacob?

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: Likening an old mountaineer to the biblical Jacob, who dreamt of a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob suggests the biblical patriarch and his ladder, which fits 'climber'; here it is the Jacob, a breed of spotted sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sheep; the Jacob is a piebald sheep breed, so a Jacob is sheeplike.

clue.text: Escape exam as fast as possible

parts.note: to flee is to escape
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A student running from an exam at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of the poetic adjective fleet, meaning swift, so quickest of all.

clue.text: Rather dull, getting flatter

definitions.meaning: bland plus the suffix -ish describes something somewhat dull
to coax someone with compliments and smooth talk

explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' reads as the comparative of flat, matching 'dull'; it is the verb, to praise insincerely.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax with smooth talk and compliments, a near synonym of the verb flatter.

clue.text: Knitted cashmere? I don't know

indicators.note: knitted wool is worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether a jumper is knitted cashmere shrugs that they have no idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial phrase used to say you have no idea of the answer, so it equals a shrug.

clue.text: Screen employees coming back into agency

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: men can mean workers or employees

explanation.surface: Staff returning to a spy agency after a screening process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' wants to be a verb, as in vetting the employees; it is the noun, the silver screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The screen is a byword for films and moviegoing, so it stands for a picture house.

clue.text: What's disturbed rural blag with weapon?

definitions.text: What's disturbed rural blag with weapon?

indicators.note: disturbed means put into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Asking what interrupted an armed robbery in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A blag is British slang for a robbery. 'disturbed' rearranges RURAL BLAG, and ARM follows. Read whole, the clue asks what goes off during a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A security device that sounds when a break-in is attempted, interrupting robbers in the act.

clue.text: Hate crime, alternatively

parts.note: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a criminal offence in English law
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Describing hate crime as one thing or another.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal charge for assault causing injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest or loathe, a strong synonym of the verb hate.

clue.text: Disgusted after losing rugby, Pacific nation gets sedentary

indicators.note: after losing means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: Nauru is a small island nation in the Pacific
RU is the abbreviation for rugby union
seated means sitting down, sedentary

explanation.surface: A Pacific island loses at rugby and its people turn into couch potatoes, much to someone's disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sick with revulsion, so disgusted in the strong sense of being repelled.

clue.text: Pitch drink containers in bins

parts.note: a sports pitch is a field
glasses hold drinks

explanation.surface: Throwing drinks glasses into the rubbish bins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bins' looks like rubbish bins, matching 'Pitch' as throw; it is British slang for binoculars.
explanation.definitionFit: Binoculars, informally called bins in Britain, are also known by this outdoor name.

clue.text: Reported cane toad swimming on top of lake

indicators.note: in a down answer, on top of puts the first piece above the second
swimming suggests movement and disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A sighting of a cane toad swimming across the surface of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges CANE TOAD, and 'on top of' sets that above L in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that is anecdotal is based on stories people have reported rather than on proper study.

clue.text: Shilling and cents repay search through rubbish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for a shilling, the old British coin
to avenge a wrong is to repay it

explanation.surface: Coins and revenge mixed with rooting through bins for loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth twelve pence, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals and people scavenge when they hunt through waste for anything usable.

clue.text: Outside broadcasts restored in secret?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for an outside broadcast, so OBS is the plural
cured means healed, restored to health

explanation.surface: Location broadcasts being secretly repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden from view is concealed, as a thing kept in secret is; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Chippendale, say, for PM?

definitions.meaning: Thomas Chippendale was a famous English furniture craftsman
a prime minister appoints and forms the government's top team of ministers

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: the PM literally makes the Cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A joiner of fine furniture, and playfully the prime minister who assembles the Cabinet.

clue.text: Approach from company's restricted by legislation

indicators.note: restricted by means held inside something else

parts.note: an Act of Parliament is a piece of legislation
CO is the abbreviation for company, and with the apostrophe s it gives COS

explanation.surface: A firm's approach being limited by new laws.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them, often boldly or aggressively.

clue.text: British football team in Lyon getting medal

parts.note: onze is French for eleven, the number in a football side

explanation.surface: A British side playing in Lyon and winning a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Third place in Olympic-style events wins a medal made of this copper alloy.

clue.text: The opposite of bad poet being listened to

parts.note: vice is wickedness, the bad as opposed to virtue

indicators.note: being listened to means we hear the sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a verser is one who writes verse, a poet

explanation.surface: A bad poet whose work is the opposite of what anyone wants to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: VERSER, a non-rhotic British pronunciation, sounds like VERSA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means the other way round, used when saying the reverse is also true.

clue.text: Opinions on western society are competing

parts.note: people who are competing vie with each other

explanation.surface: Views on Western society clash with one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's views are the beliefs or judgements they hold, just like opinions.

clue.text: Doctor welcoming green colour scheme

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: A doctor choosing a green colour scheme for the surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Interior decoration, including the choice of paint and furnishings, of a room.

clue.text: Cross Noah initially put in his boat?

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Noah

parts.note: Noah's boat was the Ark, so to put creatures into it is jokingly to ark them

explanation.surface: Asking whether Noah was the first to board his own vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' could be a verb, as in crossing the flood; it is the adjective, meaning annoyed. NARKED is British slang for irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritated or annoyed, in informal British use, is the same as being cross.

clue.text: Depressed players dropped

parts.note: the cast of a play is its players
down means fallen or dropped

explanation.surface: Actors who were dropped from the production feel low.
explanation.definitionFit: To be downcast or dejected is to be low in spirits, which is depressed.

clue.text: Tip remains of cigarette in a line on page

parts.note: a tip is an end
ash is what is left after a cigarette burns

explanation.surface: Stubbing out a cigarette and leaving a line of ash on a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' wants to be a verb, to tip ash; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A short typographical dash, wider than a hyphen, used in printed text for ranges.

clue.text: Tiresome letters featuring what one had for lunch?

indicators.note: featuring means the answer appears within the clue words

explanation.surface: Boring letters describing someone's lunch menu.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg dish is a common light lunch, so this is one example of a midday meal.
